title: Dee Andros: OU Guard Turned Oregon State Giant Killer
question: Which former Oklahoma Sooners lineman coached Oregon State's 1967 Giant Killers?
answer: Dee Andros, a guard at Oklahoma from 1946 to 1949 under Bud Wilkinson, coached Oregon State from 1965 to 1975. His 1967 team beat No. 2 Purdue and top-ranked USC and became known as the Giant Killers.
summary: Dee Andros played guard for Bud Wilkinson's Sooners, then coached Oregon State's 1967 Giant Killers and later served as the school's athletic director.
body: Dee Andros played guard at the University of Oklahoma from 1946 to 1949, in the early years of Bud Wilkinson's run in Norman. He was an Oklahoma native, and after his playing days he stayed in the game as a coach, building a resume that included a stretch as an assistant on Wilkinson's staff.

From there he worked his way up through college assistant jobs at several programs before becoming a head coach, first at Idaho beginning in 1962 and then at Oregon State, where he arrived in 1965 and stayed through the 1975 season.

His signature year came in 1967. Oregon State finished 7-2-1 and earned the nickname the Giant Killers after beating No. 2 Purdue and then knocking off top-ranked USC 3-0 at Parker Stadium. Andros was also a fixture in the Civil War rivalry with Oregon, winning nine of eleven meetings.

When his coaching run ended, Andros moved into the athletic director's chair at Oregon State, where he led fundraising efforts and remained until he retired in 1985. Sources differ slightly on the exact year he took the job, so we only say he served through 1985. Oregon State inducted him into its athletics hall of fame in 1991.
It is a good reminder that Wilkinson-era Sooners carried the lessons of Norman into coaching offices all over the country.
